definitions.explanation: A proposed plan for a project, event, or product, typically written up for review and approval. Compound of {企画|きかく} (planning) + {案|あん} (proposal, draft).

examples.japanese: {企画案|きかくあん}を{出|だ}す。
{会議|かいぎ}で{新|あたら}しい{企画案|きかくあん}を{説明|せつめい}した。
examples.english: I explained the new project proposal at the meeting.

examples.japanese: {部長|ぶちょう}に{企画案|きかくあん}を{何度|なんど}も{書|か}き{直|なお}すように{言|い}われた。
examples.english: The department head told me to rewrite the project proposal many times.

notes:
Common in business: a written proposal for an event, campaign, or new product that is presented for approval. The {案|あん} suffix marks it as a draft idea still open to revision.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {企画案|きかくあん}を{出|だ}す・{提出|ていしゅつ}する: to submit a proposal
- {企画案|きかくあん}を{練|ね}る: to work out / refine a proposal
- {企画案|きかくあん}が{通|とお}る: a proposal is approved

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {改善案|かいぜんあん}: improvement proposal — focuses on fixing an existing situation
- {提案|ていあん}: proposal, suggestion — the general act of proposing
